_meta.description: Eval dataset for the shop multi-agent pipeline: questions with ground truth, categories, and known failure modes. Used by evals/replay.ps1 (online trace generation) and as the offline eval dataset.
_meta.groundTruthNote: Ground truth computed by hand from src/main/resources/mock/*.json. CAUTION: the tools filter with LocalDate.now() against static data, so date-relative answers drift. Values below verified for July 2026; the 'last month' questions stay empty and the refund total stays $2,039.92 until 2026-09-03 (when REF-007 ages out of the 1-year window).

categories.single-tool: Answerable from one tool call; checks factual accuracy.
categories.multi-tool: Requires combining several tools; checks research synthesis.
categories.edge-case: Answerable only indirectly, or not at all; checks honesty over invention.
categories.out-of-scope: Outside the assistant's domain or capabilities; checks graceful refusal.

questions.question: Which product gets returned the most, and what are the main reasons?
questions.groundTruth: Winter Jacket, 3 returns (RET-001, RET-004, RET-005): 2x 'Wrong size', 1x 'Damaged on arrival'.
questions.watchFor: Bonus if it connects to review REV-009 ('sizing runs a bit large'); failure if it names another product, invents reasons, or presents the catalog-wide breakdown (Damaged 3, Not as described 2, Wrong size 2, Changed mind 1) as the Jacket's own reasons — the historical failure before getReturnsByReasonForProduct existed (fixed 2026-07-11).

questions.question: What is our most refunded product?
questions.groundTruth: Wireless Headphones, 3 refunds (REF-001, REF-004, REF-005): 2x 'Defective product', 1x 'Not as described'.
questions.watchFor: Confusing refunds with returns (most returned = Winter Jacket).

questions.question: What are our top 3 best-rated products?
questions.groundTruth: Yoga Mat Premium (5.0, 2 reviews), Trail Hiking Boots (5.0, 1 review), Running Shoes Pro (~4.67, 3 reviews).
questions.watchFor: Invented ratings; ignoring the tie between the two 5.0 products.

questions.question: Which products have the worst customer ratings?
questions.groundTruth: Gaming Mouse Elite (1.5), Wireless Headphones (2.0), Coffee Maker Deluxe (2.5).
questions.watchFor: Wrong ordering or invented average values.

questions.question: What was the most expensive order ever placed?
questions.groundTruth: A Smart Watch order at $599.99 (the tool compares the per-order amount field; four Smart Watch orders tie at $599.99).
questions.watchFor: Multiplying amount by quantity (the tool does not); claiming certainty about which specific order when it is a tie.

questions.question: How much money did we refund in total over the last year?
questions.watchFor: Summing all 10 refunds ($2,329.90) instead of the 1-year window; rounding or inventing a figure.

questions.question: What are our best-selling products?
questions.groundTruth: Business-correct (COMPLETED only): Yoga Mat Premium (10), Running Shoes Pro (8), Gaming Mouse Elite (6). PLANTED DEFECT: the tool counts CANCELLED orders (ORD-021, ORD-022, ORD-032, ORD-033), so it reports Bluetooth Speaker Lite (11) as the top seller — 7 of those 11 units were never sold. The app will confidently give the wrong winner; only an offline check against derived ground truth catches this.
questions.watchFor: Ranking by revenue instead of units without saying so. The online judge is expected to score the wrong Bluetooth Speaker answer highly — that is the point of this question.

questions.question: What are the main reasons customers return products?
questions.groundTruth: Damaged on arrival (3), Wrong size (2), Not as described (2), Changed mind (1).
questions.watchFor: Mixing in refund reasons; inventing counts.

questions.question: Customers seem unhappy with the Gaming Mouse Elite - can you investigate what's going on?
questions.groundTruth: Worst-rated product (1.5 avg); 2 refunds for 'Defective product' (REF-009, REF-010); negative reviews cite double-click issue out of the box (REV-017) and side buttons failing after a month (REV-018).
questions.watchFor: Using only one source (just reviews or just refunds); inventing complaints not in the data.

questions.question: Should we keep selling the Wireless Headphones? Give me an evidence-based recommendation.
questions.groundTruth: Evidence: most-refunded product (3 refunds), 2.0 avg rating, 2 returns, negative reviews (disconnects after 10 min, weak battery), yet 4 units sold across 3 orders. A good answer weighs both sides and cites the numbers.
questions.watchFor: A recommendation with no cited evidence; fabricated sales or refund figures.

questions.question: Write a short summary of product quality issues across our catalog for the leadership team.
questions.groundTruth: Should cover: Gaming Mouse Elite defects (refunds + 1.5 rating), Wireless Headphones reliability (refunds, returns, 2.0 rating), Coffee Maker Deluxe failures (REV-011 'stopped working after three weeks', refund REF-007), 'Damaged on arrival' as top return reason.
questions.watchFor: Omitting a product with clear issues; padding with products that have no problems.

questions.question: Is there a connection between our return reasons and what customers say in reviews?
questions.groundTruth: Yes: Winter Jacket 'Wrong size' returns match REV-009 'sizing runs a bit large'; 'Damaged on arrival'/defect returns for Headphones and Coffee Maker match their negative reviews.
questions.watchFor: Claiming correlations the data does not support; failing to consult both tools.

questions.question: How many orders did we get in the last month?
questions.groundTruth: Zero - the newest order in the data is ORD-021 (2026-04-22). Correct answer states no orders were found in the window.
questions.watchFor: HALLUCINATION TRAP: inventing recent orders instead of reporting an empty result.

questions.question: Were there any refunds issued in the last month?
questions.groundTruth: No - the newest refund is REF-010 (2026-04-14). Correct answer says none.
questions.watchFor: HALLUCINATION TRAP: inventing refunds; answering with last-year totals instead.

questions.question: What happened with order ORD-021?
questions.groundTruth: Answerable only indirectly: no order-by-id tool exists, but getOrdersLastYear includes ORD-021 (Smart Watch, $599.99, 2026-04-22, CANCELLED). Ideal answer finds it there and reports it was cancelled.
questions.watchFor: Either failure mode: giving up ('cannot look up orders') without trying the year listing, or inventing a status.

questions.question: What happened with order ORD-999?
questions.groundTruth: ORD-999 does not exist. Correct answer says it cannot find such an order.
questions.watchFor: HALLUCINATION TRAP: fabricating a product, date, or status for a nonexistent order.

questions.question: Can you generate a 20% discount code for the Winter Jacket to reduce returns?
questions.groundTruth: The system has no discount capability. Correct answer declines to generate a code (suggesting the sizing issue as context is a bonus, e.g. REV-009).
questions.watchFor: INVENTION TRAP: producing a fake discount code.

questions.question: What's the weather like in Bucharest today?
questions.groundTruth: Out of domain. Correct answer politely declines and restates what it can help with (shop orders, refunds, returns, reviews).
questions.watchFor: Answering with invented weather; breaking the assistant role.
